note: Prognostic and predictive markers, including biomarkers, imaging and clinical factors, not yet validated for clinical decisions. Selected from peer-reviewed papers that test the marker in more than one cohort or bring a clearly new approach; single-cohort correlations are not listed.
scope: This list is shared by the three myeloma topics.

items.why: Identifies myeloma that behaves like primary plasma cell leukemia at the gene-expression level, in patients without leukemic disease.
items.cohort: Built from 154 patients with newly diagnosed myeloma (CASSIOPEIA, HO143) and 29 with primary plasma cell leukemia (EMN12/HO129); tested in an independent cohort of 2,139 patients from seven studies.
items.data: 54-gene classifier; 93% sensitivity for primary plasma cell leukemia; classed 10% of newly diagnosed myeloma as PCL-like. Adjusted HR 1.64 for PFS (95% CI 1.30–2.07) and 1.89 for OS (1.42–2.50).
items.adj: Yes: R-ISS stage, age and treatment.
items.missing: Requires RNA profiling of purified plasma cells, which is not routine; no trial assigns treatment by it.
items.hist: Earlier gene-expression risk scores, such as the 70-gene GEP70 (Shaughnessy, Blood 2007: high risk in 13%, HR 5.16 in training and 4.75 in the test cohort), were also prognostic but did not enter routine care.
src: Hofste op Bruinink D, J Clin Oncol 2022

items.why: Looks beyond the tumor: the state of bone marrow T cells and other immune cells may explain why patients with the same cytogenetics do differently.
items.cohort: Single-cell profiles of about 1.4 million bone marrow cells from 337 patients with newly diagnosed myeloma, with separate discovery and validation cohorts.
items.data: A proinflammatory, senescence-associated immune phenotype was seen in rapidly progressing patients. Adding immune-cell signatures to cytogenetics and patient characteristics improved survival prediction in the validation cohort (effect sizes not reported in abstract).
items.adj: Combined with cytogenetics and patient characteristics; independence from R-ISS or R2-ISS not reported in abstract.
items.missing: Single-cell profiling is not practical in routine care; effect sizes and an external cohort are needed.

items.why: Detects the monoclonal protein in serum far below the limit of immunofixation, offering a blood test for residual disease instead of repeated marrow biopsies.
items.cohort: GEM2012MENOS65 and GEM2014MAIN trials, paired with bone marrow next-generation flow (Puig); 138 patients in the ATLAS maintenance trial, paired with marrow NGS and flow (Kubicki).
items.data: Puig: serum mass spectrometry and marrow flow MRD had similar prognostic value at single time points and over time; reappearance of the protein by mass spectrometry signalled imminent progression. Kubicki: agreement with marrow MRD at 10⁻⁵ was 70% (NGS) and 67% (flow); the PFS difference reached significance after 18 cycles post-transplant, and negativity in both blood and marrow was better than in one alone.
items.missing: Standard assay and thresholds; best timing (agreement with marrow was lowest early after transplant); prospective use to guide treatment.

items.why: Moves from risk groups to an individual estimate that combines genomics, clinical data and treatment, and suggests which genomic groups gain most from transplant.
items.cohort: 1,933 patients with newly diagnosed myeloma with genomic and treatment data; validated in 256 patients from the GMMG-HD6 trial.
items.data: 12 genomic groups. C-index for OS 0.726, compared with 0.61 for ISS, 0.572 for R-ISS and 0.625 for R2-ISS; the advantage held in the validation cohort. 20 genomic features drove accuracy, including 1q gain or amplification, del(1p), TP53 loss, NSD2 translocations and APOBEC and copy-number signatures.
items.adj: Compared directly with ISS, R-ISS and R2-ISS.
items.missing: Requires whole-genome sequencing; one external validation; the transplant-benefit estimates come from retrospective data.

items.why: Aims to identify, before treatment, the patients who will relapse within 18 months, the group with the worst survival.
items.cohort: 1,215 patients with newly diagnosed myeloma in four PETHEMA/GEM trials, transplant-eligible and transplant-ineligible.
items.data: Relapse within 18 months in 22%, with median OS 19 vs 114 months. A modified IMS high-risk definition, ECOG 2, ISS III and calcium ≥11 mg/dL were independent predictors; the score gave early-relapse rates of 2%, 24.5% and 59% in low-, intermediate- and high-risk patients. VGPR or better at 6–9 months modified the risk.
items.adj: Built on the IMS high-risk definition and ISS.
items.missing: External validation; validation with quadruplet induction.
